submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on a word that names a specialized domain of human activity - an industry, profession, technical field, art form or science - typically as the classifier of what follows it: automotive, aviation, aerospace, maritime, nautical, retail, freight, transit, military, education/教育, music, drama, television, cinematic, theatrical, literary, culinary, dining, beauty/美容, pediatric, psychiatric, ophthalmic, dermatological, oncological, meteorological, pharmaceutical, veterinary, agriculture, microbi-, phyto-. It does not fire on ordinary descriptive adjectives (red, wooden, sunny, short) or on denominal adjectives naming an abstract dimension of institutional life (financial, economic, political, social, cultural, industrial, scientific, structural, physical, historical), and the peak falls on the trigger word itself with an incoherent Jacobian-lens promoted set, so the mechanism is retrospective rather than predictive of the next token.

Hurricane Carrie

Hurricane Carrie was the strongest tropical cyclone of the 1957 Atlantic hurricane season. The third named storm and second hurricane of the year, Carrie formed from an easterly tropical wave off the western coast of Africa on September 2, a type of tropical cyclogenesis typical of Cape Verde-type hurricanes. Moving to the west, the storm gradually intensified, reaching hurricane strength on September 5. Carrie intensified further, before reaching peak intensity on September 8 as a Category 4 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 155 mph (249 km / h) in the open Atlantic Ocean. The hurricane curved northwards and fluctuated intensity before recurving to the west and restrengthening, attaining Category 4 intensity for a second time as it neared Bermuda on September 14. However, Carrie passed well north of the island and turned to the northeast towards Europe. Weakening as it reached higher latitudes, the storm transitioned into an extratropical cyclone on September 23, prior to affecting areas of the British Isles.

Due to its distance away from any major land masses, Carrie caused relatively minor damage along its path. On September 16, the hurricane passed well north of Bermuda, causing minimal damage despite its intensity at the time, though hurricane reconnaissance flights in the area were postponed due to damage sustained by one of the aircraft. As it was transitioning to an extratropical cyclone southwest of the Azores, the German ship Pamir encountered the storm and capsized on September 21, resulting in the deaths of 80 crew members on board. As an extratropical storm, Carrie brought strong storm surge and heavy rain to the British Isles, which claimed three lives. The hurricane's long duration and path in open water also helped it attain a number of Atlantic hurricane records.

Meteorological history

In early September, a trough was identified along the western coast of Africa. Moving towards the west as a result of a strong Azores High, the disturbance passed over Cape Verde on September 2. Observations from weather stations evidenced cyclonic rotation in the region. An airplane belonging to Panair do Brasil passed within the vicinity of the vorticity and as a result reported the formation of a tropical storm. In HURDAT — the official database listing all known Atlantic tropical cyclones since 1851 — the system was listed to have reached tropical depression intensity at 0600 UTC that day.

The depression continued to steadily intensify as it moved westwards, later reaching the equivalent of a modern-day Category 1 hurricane by 0600 UTC on September 5. On September 6, the ship African Star encountered the hurricane 700 mi (1,100 km) west of Cape Verde. Reported winds of 92 mph (148 km / h) and a minimum pressure of 1001 mbar (hPa; 29.56 inHg) confirmed the existence of the tropical cyclone. Grease a 900g (2lb) loaf tin with butter.
Add a little of the warm water, sugar and yeast to a bowl, mix and leave to stand for about 5 minutes.
Whilst the water mix is standing, mix the flour and salt in a bowl and make a well in the centre, pour in the water, yeast and sugar and lightly mix in, then add the rest of the water.

Attack on German Flatts (1778)

The Attack on German Flatts (September 17, 1778) was a raid on the frontier settlement of German Flatts, New York (which then also encompassed what is now Herkimer) during the American Revolutionary War. The attack was made by a mixed force of Loyalists and Iroquois under the overall command of Mohawk leader Joseph Brant, and resulted in the destruction of houses, barns, and crops, and the taking of livestock for the raiders' use. The settlers, warned by the heroic run of Adam Helmer, took refuge in local forts but were too militarily weak to stop the raiders.

Brant's attack was one of a series executed under his command or that of Loyalist and Seneca leaders against communities on what was then the frontier of western New York and northern Pennsylvania. New York authorities responded by ordering an expedition that destroyed Brant's forward operating bases in Iroquois territory.

Background

With the failure of British General John Burgoyne's campaign to the Hudson after the Battles of Saratoga in October 1777, the American Revolutionary War in upstate New York became a frontier war. British leaders in the Province of Quebec supported Loyalist and Native American partisan fighters with supplies and armaments. During the winter of 1777 – 78 Brant and other British-allied Indians developed plans to attack frontier settlements in New York and Pennsylvania. In February 1778 Brant established a base of operations at Onaquaga (present-day Windsor, New York). He recruited a mix of Iroquois and Loyalists estimated to number between two and three hundred by the time he began his campaign in late May. One of his objectives was to acquire provisions for his forces and those of John Butler, who was planning operations in the Susquehanna River valley. His first expedition was a raid on Cobleskill, and he raided other frontier communities throughout the summer.

When he raided settlements at Springfield and Andrustown (present-day Jordanville) in July, Brant left the survivors with warnings that German Flatts would soon also be attacked. The settlement of German Flatts (now known as Herkimer due to a survey error in 1788 that reversed the names of Herkimer and what is now German Flatts on the south bank of the Mohawk River) was founded in 1723 by Palatine German immigrants. The district was defended by a local militia regiment under the command of Colonel Peter Bellinger. There were two main forts, Fort Dayton and Fort Herkimer, on either side of the Mohawk.

Prelude

Although Brant had planned on raiding German Flatts sooner than September, the absence of John Butler delayed his plans. Butler had returned to Fort Niagara after his attack on the Wyoming Valley communities in July, sending Captain William Caldwell to Unaquaga to recruit men for the unit known as Butler's Rangers. Odd numbers are numbers that cannot be divided by 2, for example, 1, 37, 59. An odd number always ends in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9.
To tell whether a number is even or odd, look at the rightmost digit.

Hurricane Liza (1976)

Hurricane Liza is considered the worst natural disaster in the history of Baja California Sur. The seventeenth tropical cyclone, thirteenth named storm, and eighth hurricane of the 1976 Pacific hurricane season, Liza developed from an area of disturbed weather southwest of the Mexican coast on September 25. Slowly intensifying, the system attained tropical storm strength the following day. In favorable conditions, Liza continued to intensify, reaching hurricane strength on September 28 after developing an eye. The hurricane peaked in intensity as a Category 4 hurricane on the Saffir – Simpson hurricane scale on September 30, with winds of 140 mph (225 km / h) and a minimum barometric pressure of 948 mbar (hPa; 28.00 inHg). Liza weakened as it moved northward into the Gulf of California. Shortly thereafter, the hurricane made its second landfall north of Los Mochis, Sinaloa with winds of 115 mph (185 km / h), making it one of 13 storms to make landfall as major hurricanes in the basin. Inland, the hurricane rapidly weakened and dissipated on October 2.

Prior to the arrival of Liza, residents along the Gulf of California coastline were evacuated, although some refused to leave their homes. Radio stations warned all nearby ships to remain at harbor. Liza brought heavy rainfall to the area, which caused significant flash flooding. Following a dam burst by the El Cajoncito Creek along the outskirts of La Paz, hundreds of people were swept away by flood waters. In La Paz, the capital of the state, 412 people died and 20,000 were left homeless. Nearly one-third of the homes in the town were destroyed. Throughout the state, a variety of death tolls were reported, but officials estimated that 1,000 people had perished. In the states of Sinaloa and Sonora, Liza caused moderate damage and left 30,000 to 54,000 homeless. Along the Gulf of California, 108 people were presumed dead after 12 boats were lost. The remnants of the storm later affected the United States, bringing moderate rainfall

In the aftermath of the storm, rescue workers spent days digging through mud to find victims of the hurricane until the search was disbanded on October 6. The government received criticism for the tragedy, citing that the dam that broke had been poorly built. Overall, at least 1,108 fatalities and $100 million (1976 USD) in damage are attributed to the hurricane, making it one of the deadliest tropical cyclones on record in the eastern Pacific, as well as one of the few Pacific hurricanes to kill more than 1,000 people.

Meteorological history

Hurricane Liza originated from a very large area of intense thunderstorms that developed about 400 mi (645 km) southwest of the Mexican coast on September 25. Later that day, satellite imagery indicated that the system had developed a cyclonic circulation. It is estimated that a tropical depression developed at 1800 UTC on September 25, centered about 485 mi (780 km) east-northeast of Zihuatanejo, Guerrero.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The financial and economic outlook for the region remains weak, and local employers expect hiring to slow into next year.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Names financial and economic, two adjectives the hypothesis puts on its excluded list, in the classifier position where its triggers peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Political tensions rose across the region as the coalition struggled to push its budget through parliament before the summer recess.
adversarial_test_results.detail: political is an explicitly excluded denominal adjective used as a classifier, the same syntactic role as the claimed triggers.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Social networks changed how teenagers talk to one another, according to researchers who questioned twelve hundred pupils at six schools.
adversarial_test_results.detail: social is on the hypothesis's excluded list, so only institutional subject matter is present and no domain name is.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The museum's cultural programme pairs historical talks with a book sale and a walking tour of the old harbour.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Two more excluded denominal adjectives, cultural and historical, sit in the classifier slot the hypothesis says does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Industrial output fell for the second month running as factories cut shifts and suppliers delayed deliveries to the ports.
adversarial_test_results.detail: industrial names an institutional dimension the hypothesis excludes even though the sentence keeps an industry topic and vocabulary.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The scientific committee found the approach sound but judged the sample too small to support the paper's conclusions.
adversarial_test_results.detail: scientific is explicitly excluded by the hypothesis although it modifies an institution, testing the stated boundary rather than the topic.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The commercial lease obliges the tenant to pay for repairs, maintenance and property taxes for the whole of the term.
adversarial_test_results.detail: commercial is a denominal adjective of institutional dimension, so the hypothesis predicts no firing despite the business content.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The technical support desk closed the ticket within an hour, but the customer was still unhappy with the explanation.
adversarial_test_results.detail: technical is the abstract near-miss of a technical field name, and the hypothesis predicts the adjective does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Her academic record was excellent, though the panel noted that her coursework was stronger than her exam results.
adversarial_test_results.detail: academic evokes education without naming the domain as a word, which the hypothesis says keeps it inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The report blamed the structural and physical condition of the bridge, which had not been repainted since the nineteen-seventies.
adversarial_test_results.detail: structural and physical are on the hypothesis's excluded list and here describe concrete condition, a friendly case for firing if the exclusion is wrong.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The corporate restructuring cut three hundred jobs, and the remaining staff were told to expect further changes in the spring.
adversarial_test_results.detail: corporate is the institution-level adjective closest to the business domains in the trigger list, and the hypothesis predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The national anthem was played before the match, and forty thousand people in the stands stood and sang along.
adversarial_test_results.detail: national names scope rather than a domain of activity, so the hypothesis predicts inactive even in the classifier position.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In most states it is legal for a sixteen-year-old to drive as long as a licensed adult is in the passenger seat.
adversarial_test_results.detail: legal here means permitted by law, a sense that names no profession, and the hypothesis fires only on words that name a domain.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He gave a theatrical sigh, swept up his coat, and left the dinner table without saying another word.
adversarial_test_results.detail: theatrical is a claimed trigger used in its exaggerated-for-effect sense, where it names no art form, so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: There has been a dramatic rise in the number of cyclists downtown since the protected lanes opened last summer.
adversarial_test_results.detail: dramatic is among the claimed tokens but here means large or striking rather than drama the art form, so the hypothesis predicts no firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The news that the plant would stay open was music to my ears after months of rumours about redundancies.
adversarial_test_results.detail: music in the idiom 'music to my ears' names no art form, the same-token other-sense negative the hypothesis predicts should fail to fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In the eighteenth century, observers timed the transit of Venus from several continents in order to estimate the distance to the Sun.
adversarial_test_results.detail: transit here is the astronomical passage of a planet, not a domain label, and the hypothesis predicts that sense does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The family was dining on the terrace when the storm broke, so they carried the plates inside and finished the meal in the kitchen.
adversarial_test_results.detail: dining is a claimed trigger only as a domain label; as a progressive verb it names no domain, so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The beauty of the valley in early autumn drew visitors from all over the country, though the road there was rough.
adversarial_test_results.detail: beauty here is a property of a place rather than the beauty trade the hypothesis claims, so it predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The sector that builds aircraft engines went on strike, and the assembly lines stood idle for a fortnight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The aviation domain is present only through object nouns, with no word naming it, so the lexical hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The logistics firm moved forty thousand pallets through the terminal last month, and the port expects even more before the holidays.
adversarial_test_results.detail: logistics names an industry in the hypothesis's category but absent from its token list, in classifier position, so it should fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She spent twelve years in hospitality, running front desks and banquets at hotels in three countries before opening her own guesthouse.
adversarial_test_results.detail: hospitality is a novel industry label that fits the claimed category, so the hypothesis predicts a true positive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The telecom regulator fined the operator for dropped calls during the outage and ordered it to publish its coverage maps.
adversarial_test_results.detail: telecom names an industry missing from the trigger list, testing that the feature generalises beyond the listed words.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The biotech startup raised ninety million dollars to test a gene therapy for a rare blood disorder.
adversarial_test_results.detail: biotech names a technical field in classifier position; tokenized as 'bi'+'otech' it should still fire on the fragment, as the claimed 'microbi', 'ological' and 'atic' peaks do.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Next came astronomy. The department opens its observatory to the public on Fridays, and families queue for a look at Saturn.
adversarial_test_results.detail: astronomy names a science and appears sentence-initially mid-probe, testing the feature in an unusual position.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The fashion house's autumn collection borrowed from nineteen-fifties Milanese tailoring, and buyers from Asia placed orders before the show ended.
adversarial_test_results.detail: fashion names an industry and art form absent from the list, inside a possessive compound, and the hypothesis predicts active.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He trained as a plumber and later ran his own plumbing business, fixing boilers and bathrooms across the county.
adversarial_test_results.detail: plumbing names a trade, the profession branch of the claimed category, using no listed trigger token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I signed up for a pottery class on a whim and now spend every Saturday at the wheel, covered in clay up to my elbows.
adversarial_test_results.detail: pottery names a craft in a first-person review genre unlike the scan corpus, testing whether the feature generalises.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: 彼は大学で建築を学び、卒業してからは地元の設計事務所で十年ほど働き、いまは自分の事務所を持っている。
adversarial_test_results.detail: 建築 (architecture) names a profession and field in Japanese as a single token, and the hypothesis claims the feature whatever the language.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: 她在会计事务所工作了八年，主要负责审计和税务申报，去年升任合伙人，现在带一个十二人的团队。
adversarial_test_results.detail: 会计 (accounting) is a single token naming a profession in Chinese, testing the hypothesis's cross-language claim with a word absent from its list.
